page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) mapped from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. Virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance split between single-core and multi-core workloads. Single-core execution is a relative bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all scoring in the weak category, representing the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Conversely, multi-core and parallelized execution profiles perform in the average tier, representing the middle 50%. This is demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 13975.48, a Geekbench multi-core score of 7299.0, and a Passmark CPU score of 15380.43. Memory bandwidth also sits consistently in the average tier, reaching 780.06 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 88.67 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.c6.4xlarge offers a compute-focused resource profile. The lack of bundled local storage means storage costs are externalized to network volumes, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. The instance delivers average cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads that can leverage its 16 dedicated vCPUs, but it is less efficient for single-threaded tasks due to its lower single-core performance. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded web serving, software compilation, database operations, and parallelized batch processing tasks that do not require local high-speed storage or GPU acceleration.
